skill.name: starknet-js
skill.description: Build Starknet applications with starknet.js v9 patterns for providers, accounts, contracts, transactions, fees, wallets, paymasters, and Cairo data types.
skill.summary: Practical starknet.js v9 guidance for reliable Starknet reads, signed transactions, wallet flows, and sponsored execution.

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, expected Starknet RPC examples, or standard local signer setup. The run instruction places a private key in a shell command, creating a credential exposure risk.

remediation.issue: Private key shown as an inline shell environment assignment
remediation.suggestion: Use protected secret injection or a managed signer, and document placeholder configuration without placing private keys in shell command history.

content.value_statement: Starknet development requires careful handling of providers, accounts, fees, and Cairo data types. This skill provides focused starknet.js v9 patterns for common workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates provider and contract interaction patterns for reading Starknet state.
Guides account setup, deployment, signing, transaction execution, simulation, and receipt checks.
Explains fee estimation, resource bounds, priority tips, and paymaster transactions.
Shows wallet connections, multicalls, typed contracts, event parsing, and SNIP-12 message signing.
Covers Cairo calldata helpers, BigInt token amounts, ERC-20 operations, and contract deployment.
Provides provider hardening, account lifecycle, and fee policy guidance for production agents.
limitations: Targets starknet.js v9.x and may require updates for other SDK versions.
Does not author Cairo contracts or perform smart contract security audits.
Example endpoints and class hashes must be verified before production use.
Signed transaction examples require user-managed credentials and funded accounts.

use_cases.title: Add Starknet Wallet Flows
use_cases.description: Connect browser wallets, react to account changes, and submit transactions through WalletAccount.

use_cases.title: Build Transaction Services
use_cases.description: Configure providers, accounts, fee estimation, simulation, execution, and receipt monitoring.

use_cases.title: Implement Advanced Account Features
use_cases.description: Design paymaster, multicall, message signing, deployment, and outside execution workflows.
use_cases.target_user: Protocol engineers and account abstraction teams

prompt_templates.title: Read Contract State
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a starknet.js v9 TypeScript example that reads [method] from [contract]. Include provider setup, ABI use, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Submit a Signed Transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a signed [entrypoint] call for [account]. Include simulation, fee estimation, calldata construction, execution, and receipt status checks.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a Wallet and Paymaster
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a wallet flow for [application] using [network]. Add account changes, paymaster fee options, approval steps, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Harden an Automated Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Starknet workflow for provider failover, nonce conflicts, fee limits, signer boundaries, replay protection, and transaction monitoring: [workflow].

output_examples.input: Read an ERC-20 balance without losing numeric precision.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering provider creation, contract connection, BigInt balance handling, decimal formatting, and RPC error reporting.
A workflow that builds both calls, checks paymaster support, estimates fees, confirms sponsor policy, executes once, and monitors the receipt.

output_examples.input: Diagnose a transaction that reverted after submission.
output_examples.output: A review of receipt status, revert reason, simulation output, calldata, fee bounds, nonce state, and network selection.

best_practices: Verify chain ID, RPC endpoint, account class hash, and SDK version before signing or submitting transactions.
Simulate calls and estimate fees before execution, then enforce explicit spending and sponsorship limits.
Keep private keys outside prompts, logs, shell history, and source files; use managed signers or protected secret injection.
anti_patterns: Do not convert token balances or fees to JavaScript Number values.
Do not submit transactions with unverified network, calldata, fee bounds, or paymaster policy.
Do not embed private keys, production RPC credentials, or real account secrets in examples.

faq.question: Which starknet.js version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It targets starknet.js v9.x with Node.js 18 or later and TypeScript 5 or later.

faq.question: Can this skill write Cairo contracts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on TypeScript SDK integration with deployed Starknet contracts.

faq.question: Does it support browser wallets?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WalletAccount connections, account changes, network changes, and transaction submission.

faq.question: How should private keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use a managed signer or protected secret injection. Never place private keys in prompts, logs, source files, or shell commands.

faq.question: Does it cover fees and paymasters?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers estimates, resource bounds, priority tips, sponsored fees, alternative gas tokens, and policy checks.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are reference patterns. Verify endpoints, class hashes, SDK signatures, signer controls, budgets, retries, and monitoring before production use.
